chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: George Hearst on Central Avenue; Orson Welles
summary: Royal says it was George Hearst, not William Randolph, who visited the Avenue.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I've heard that -- well, William Randolph Hearst was a regular customer.

William Randolph Hearst -- it wasn't William Randolph Hearst at all. Now, you can get it straight from the horse's mouth now. George Hearst was a friend of mine and he used to come out to Sebastian's Cotton Club and ask me to take him down on Central Avenue to enjoy himself down there

at the after-hours places. So I knew George Hearst very well. William Randolph Hearst never came on the Avenue in his life because he was from some sort of affliction -- he was sort of semi-invalid. He didn't get around. He had elephantitis or something, some kind of way. He was really not a healthy man. The only thing he was really healthy in was money. But George used to come down and he was considered as being the black sheep of the family.
George. No, he was just sort of wild and went out in his different ways.
Orson Welles came around Central Avenue, did he not?
I didn't know Orson Welles as a person. So far as his coming and going, I couldn't honestly say.
I know he's a jazz fan, but I had heard that he (inaudible). used to come to the Alabam
Yeah, I don't know about him at all.
